transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well... I don't really know where to start. I guess... I got a little scared lately. Just... thinking that maybe it'd be a relief if I just didn't wake up in the morning. I haven't tried to hurt myself or nothing like that. Just... it bothered me enough to come in.
How long have you been having these thoughts about not wanting to wake up?
Well... I suppose it's been about four months now. Just... around the time my aunt came to live with us.
Have you been enjoying things you usually like to do over the past four months?

Not really... I used to look forward to my watercolors, or... going to dance class. Walking with the ladies. But... I don't know. Lately I just leave my things sitting there. I just can't seem to make myself care.
Have you experienced any loss of interest in activities that you usually find pleasurable?
I... well, like I just said... I don't really care much for my painting or the walking anymore. I just... don't have the interest.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite over the past four months?
I don't think so... I suppose I eat about the same as I always do.
Have you been having any problems with your sleep over the past four months?
Not that I've noticed. I... I sleep fine, I guess.
Have you been feeling guilty or worthless about anything lately?

I... I don't know. I guess sometimes I feel bad. Like... when I get tired or, you know, annoyed with my aunt. I just... I start thinking I'm a bad woman. Like I'm bringing shame on my family because I should be more grateful. But... I don't know.
Have you had a period of at least two weeks where you felt better and your interest in activities returned to normal over the past four months?
I don't think so. It's just... mostly been the same.
Have you had any periods where these feelings of not wanting to wake up and lack of interest in activities were really severe, almost all the time?
I... no, I wouldn't say that. It's just... it's just been how it is. Not... not worse than usual, I guess.
Have you lost any significant amount of weight over the past four months?
No... I haven't really noticed. I think my clothes still fit about the same, mostly. I don't really weigh myself.
Have you noticed yourself moving more slowly or feeling like you're speeding up in your thoughts or actions over the past four months?

I... I'm not really sure. My husband, he... he tells me I'm moving like everything takes extra effort lately. And... I guess when I go to the market, I just... I stand there for a long time before I actually pick up what I need. But... I don't feel like my thoughts are speeding up or anything.
Have you been feeling sad most of the time over the past four months?

I... I suppose so. Mostly in the mornings, anyway. I just wake up and... there's this heavy sadness right in my chest. It just feels like... like I already failed the day before it even really starts. But... yeah, I guess that's mostly how it's been.
Would you say that these feelings of sadness and not wanting to wake up are present most of the day, every day?

Well... like I just said, it's mostly the mornings. Every morning, yeah. That heavy feeling is just... it's right there when I wake up. I don't really keep track of the rest of the day. I just try to get by.
Would you say that these feelings of sadness are mild, or do they interfere significantly with your daily life?

I... I guess it gets in the way. I haven't really been doing much lately. I stopped going to my dance class... and the walking group. I don't even go to my food-pantry shifts anymore. My husband, he... he's had to take over more of the errands for me. I just... I get stuck, like I said, and I fall behind on things. So he just does it.
Would you say that your feelings of sadness are more than just a mild annoyance, but really interfere with your ability to function in daily life?

I mean... yes. Like I was just saying, I don't go to my classes or the pantry anymore. And my husband is doing all the errands. So... I guess you could say it interferes. It's... it's more than an annoyance. I just can't seem to do the things I used to.
Would you say that there are any days where you feel okay, or are the sad feelings always there?

I... I don't really know. Like I said, it's mostly the mornings. Most mornings I just wake up with this... this heavy sadness right in my chest. It feels like I already failed the day before it even starts. I don't really notice if I feel okay later on. I just... it's just there when I wake up.
Would you say that these feelings of sadness are severe enough to make it very difficult for you to do even simple tasks?

I... I thought I just said that. Yes. Even the simple things... I just fall behind. That's why I'm not doing my classes or the pantry anymore. And why my husband has to do the errands now. I just get stuck.
Would you say that your sad feelings are present every day?

I... yes, I think so. Every day. It's... like I mentioned, it's mostly the mornings. I just wake up and that heavy feeling is already there in my chest. Just... feeling like I failed before I even get out of bed. Every morning.
Would you say that your sad feelings are so severe that they make it nearly impossible for you to do even the simplest tasks most of the time?

Yes... like I just said a minute ago. It's too hard. I don't go to my dance class or the walking group anymore. I stopped my shifts at the food pantry. My husband has to do most of the errands now because... I just get stuck. I just fall behind on everything.
Would you say that your sad feelings are so severe that they nearly always make it impossible for you to do even the simplest tasks?
I... I feel like we just went over this. Yes. I can't... I don't do my dance class anymore. Or the walking group. Or the pantry. My husband does the errands. I just... I can't do them. I get stuck.
